hook: The communist who founded the People's Republic of China, whose campaigns cost tens of millions of lives.

pages.x: Mao Zedong was born in 1893 in Shaoshan, in central China, the son of a well-off peasant, and quarrelled with his strict father. He trained as a teacher, and found Marxism while working in the library of Peking University.
In 1921 he helped found the Chinese Communist Party. When Chiang Kai-shek turned on the communists in 1927, Mao led peasant fighters into the mountains, and began a guerrilla war.

In 1934 the Nationalists drove the communists from their base. On the Long March they walked some 10,000 km in a year; of 86,000 who set out, fewer than 10,000 arrived. On the way, Mao became their leader.
After fighting Japan, then Chiang's Nationalists, on 1 October 1949 Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China from the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing.

In 1958 he ordered a Great Leap Forward to overtake Britain's industry, with steel furnaces in backyards and giant farm communes. Harvests collapsed. In the famine that followed, some 15 to 45 million people died.

In 1966 he launched the Cultural Revolution. Teenage Red Guards, waving his Little Red Book, attacked teachers, officials and anything old. Temples and books were destroyed, schools closed, and hundreds of thousands died.
In 1966, aged 72, he swam in the Yangtze River at Wuhan. State newspapers claimed he swam 15 km in about an hour, which would have been a world record.
In 1972 he welcomed the American president Nixon to Beijing. He died in 1976. His portrait still hangs over the Gate of Heavenly Peace, and his body lies in a tomb on the square.
Mao united China after a century of war, but his campaigns caused the deaths of tens of millions. China's rulers say he was "70 per cent right and 30 per cent wrong".
pts: Founded the People's Republic of China
Led the Long March and the communist revolution
Tens of millions died in his famine and purges
